title: Dynamic Per-Channel Bias Compensation and Layer Offset Calibrator for Quantization Stability (Llama/Mistral/Qwen)
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: When generating FP8/INT8 profiles for Llama/Mistral/Qwen families, we observe small but persistent per-channel and per-layer mean offsets that cause accuracy regressions after quantization. These offsets differ by model family (e.g., Mistral attention matrices show asymmetric head biases, Qwen has wider residual tails in later layers, Llama shows narrow but frequent activation spikes). Existing layer-scale fixes reduce variance but do not correct systematic mean/bias shifts that accumulate across residual branches, causing generation drift on long sequences.

Proposal: Implement a two-part calibration system: 1) Dynamic Per-Channel Bias Compensation (DCBC) — compute and apply a lightweight per-channel offset correction (bias sink) during quantization calibration that is stored in the quant profile. 2) Layer Offset Calibrator (LOC) — a small deterministic post-quant transform that applies a learned scalar offset per-layer (and per-head for attention kernels where supported) to re-center activations before quant rounding. Both components are designed to be runtime-compatible (no extra forward passes during inference) and to be exportable in the profile metadata for Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.

Key algorithm details:
- Calibration dataset: 5k-step representative batches with sequence length distribution matching production (mix of 32/128/512).
- Per-channel drift detection: compute channel mean and variance across calibration set; maintain EWMA of mean with temperature smoothing to avoid reacting to single-batch spikes.
- Offset compute: if EWMA-mean deviates more than a model-family threshold (family-specific hyperparams), emit a per-channel additive offset; else zero-out to avoid noise addition.
- Stability clamp: offsets are clamped with a per-layer L2 budget to avoid over-correction; combined with residual-aware normalization to preserve layernorm behaviour in Qwen variants.
- Export format: offsets encoded as small float array in the quant profile (~KB), with metadata tags: {family, layer_idx, channel_count, calibration_seed, timestamp}.
- Interaction with kernels: update kernel quant path to optionally apply offset as bias subtraction before requantization when profile contains DCBC/LOC entries. For kernels that cannot do subtraction cheaply, fall back to adjusted scale/zero-point heuristics.

Model-specific notes:
- Llama: prioritize head-agnostic per-channel offsets in feed-forward layers; smaller offsets in attention keys/queries.
- Mistral: enable per-head LOC in attention matmuls because Mistral exhibits headwise mean shifts due to fused MHA implementation.
- Qwen: enable stronger stability clamp and residual-aware normalization (LOC applied after residual-add) because Qwen residual tails amplify mean shifts.

Validation and metrics:
- Offline eval: run 3 prompt suites (coherence, instruction-following, math/regression) plus 1k-generation fidelity checks comparing FP32 baseline vs FP8/INT8 with and without DCBC+LOC. Track delta-rejection rate >1% as failure.
- Token-level distributions: KL divergence per-layer between FP32 and quantized activation distributions before/after LOC. Target KL reduction >30% in worst layers.
- Downstream A/B: small-held-out user pool on Dedicated to validate generation regressions (<0.5% negative-feedback or rollback).

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (calibration harness): implement DCBC/LOC in calibration tool; run overnight profiles on current model catalog (Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B-v1, Qwen-14B).
- Stage 2 (kernel integration): add optional pre-quant subtract path to CPU/GPU kernels; guarded by profile flag.
- Stage 3 (canary): deploy to dedicated pool with synthetic traffic and 3-day monitoring window.
- Stage 4 (gradual): enable for Hosted for models with pass criteria met and for Private with opt-in flag.

Risks and mitigations:
- Over-correction: addressed via EWMA smoothing, clamp budgets, and family thresholds.
- Kernel performance regressions: provide heuristic to skip offset subtraction and instead adjust scale/zero-point to approximate effect on platforms where subtraction is expensive.
- Profile size growth: offsets only enabled when needed and quantized to 8-bit delta table in profile to keep size small.

Why this is different from existing layer-scale work: Existing fixes are scale-only (multiplicative). DCBC and LOC introduce an additive correction that targets mean drift independent of variance scaling, which is additive-orthogonal to previous approaches. This is particularly effective on models with residual accumulation patterns where small means accumulate into large output biases.

Operational costs: calibration run increases time by ~1.3x (extra min aggregation) and adds ~1-2 KB per-layer to profiles when offsets used.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness supports DCBC and LOC and exports offsets in profile metadata
Benchmarks show >=30% KL reduction in top-3 worst layers for Llama/Mistral/Qwen compared to baseline quant profiles
End-to-end generation delta (accuracy regressions) below 1% across evaluation suites for enabled models
Kernel path includes guarded subtract implementation without >5% throughput regression on primary GPU targets
Rollout plan documented and canary passes for at least one model family

2025-02-24 Sora Kim: Kernel prototype implemented on CUDA path; measured 2.8% throughput regression when subtract is enabled. We'll provide heuristic to only enable on layers where KL gain > threshold.
2025-02-28 QA: First sweep results attached; Llama-2-13B shows 38% KL reduction in top-5 layers, Qwen-14B shows mixed results — stronger clamp required in last 4 layers.
